text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOHA JONE
- Proceedings in the fifth anti-genocide trial against ex-senior communist officials have been delayed because of lack of witnesses.
- Two lawyers of the late communist dictator Enver Hoxha's son-in-law said they were unable to see him at the police station where he is being held.
- The Central Electoral Commission has published final results of the first round of local polls, showing a clear victory for the ruling party.
- Foreign observers will monitor Sunday's run-off of some local elections.
- The opposition Socialists' defeat in local polls reflects a crisis of trust in its leadership.

- The ruling Democrats' victory in general elections in May and June and local elections at the weekend will create problems for Albanian democracy, the leader of the ethnic Greek Human Rights Union party says.
- Electricity and kerosene will be the main sources of heating for Tirana families this winter.
- Attempts to privatise state-owned banks reveal they have lost billions of leks through bad credits. This could endanger the privatisation process.
- Russia's Gasprom is visiting Albania and may supply gas to the Balkan state.
- European Union has awrded $2.3 million to improve a road from Elbasan to Prrenjas in eastern Albania.
- Cigarette smuggling has pushed one Albanian producer to the brink of bankruptcy.
GAZETA SHQIPTARE
- Very important persons and politicians will make up Tirana district council.
RILINDJA DEMOKRATIKE
- The Democratic Party has won 88 percent of the city halls and 91 percent of the communes.
- A run-off of local elections will be held on Sunday in 22 city halls and 88 communes.
ZERI I POPULLIT
- The Socialist Party called on Albanians to vote in Sunday's run-off of local elections.
